narrative.northStar: Ember on Graphite — the catalog's own artwork glowing on woven graphite.
narrative.overview:
The world is a near-black graphite field in three tonal bands, framed above by a fixed basalt header and below by a coal footer. Panels sit one tonal step above the field behind 1px hairline seams; nothing is white. One saturated pumpkin-ember orange does all the interactive work — eyebrows, links, focus rings, the primary button — and two signature textures give the dark its depth: faint concentric thread rings plus a single soft ember glow on the hero and philosophy bands, and a large-offset structural shadow under the framed artwork card. The hero puts the catalog's own product on the first screen: the latest synced design, framed like a gallery piece beside oversized display type.

The system is a default theme, not a brand. Design Studio is a white-label product: every deployment replaces name, palette, type, and copy through configuration — the home.* studio rows drive the hero copy, philosophy band, and about teaser; the header monogram derives from the configured name's first letter. Token authority lives in the :root custom properties in app/globals.css, consumed through the Tailwind theme mapping; per-deployment theming rides on config/config.json (or the studio table) and the allow-listed themeLink stylesheet hook. Anything visual that cannot be changed from that layer is a defect.
keyCharacteristics: Three graphite bands with hairline seams; panels one tonal step up, never white
One ember hue means interactive — links, buttons, rings, eyebrows, chips
Poppins display voice over an Inter body; hierarchy by face, size, and weight
Woven-thread texture bands and the framed artwork card are the signature surfaces
Hover and focus are color shifts only; focus is a 2px ember ring
Fully token-driven and theme-swappable; zero hardcoded brand assumptions

rules.name: The No-Hardcode Rule
rules.body: Colors enter components only through the token layer (:root custom properties consumed via the Tailwind theme mapping). Literal color values are legal in exactly three places: the token definition file, the semantic green/red form-status pair, and the browser-chrome themeColor meta value in app/layout.tsx (which cannot consume a CSS variable). Nothing else may carry a literal color.

rules.name: The One Ember Rule
rules.body: Ember is the only hue that means interactive. Links, buttons, focus rings, chips, and active states all draw from it; it should stay under ~10% of any screen's pixels. If everything glows orange, nothing is clickable.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Dark surfaces separate by tonal step plus a 1px Seam border — never by white cards, never by thick strokes. A panel and its field must differ by exactly one step.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Poppins sings only in headings and card titles (font-display); Inter speaks all body copy, controls, and labels. No third family unless a deployment's theme config introduces one.

rules.name: The Color-Only Hover Rule
rules.body: Hover and focus change color, fill, or underline — never shadow. The single sanctioned transform is the design-card image zoom: hovering a card scales its media to 140% inside the clipped tile (300ms ease-out, collapsed under prefers-reduced-motion). Everything else stays a color shift; all other interactive transitions are transition-colors at ~150ms.

dos: Do source every color from the token layer — :root custom properties consumed via the Tailwind theme mapping (bg-primary, text-accent, border-input, ring-ring, bg-surface) or the primitives in components/ui/.
Do keep every deployment-specific value (name, monogram source, hero copy, philosophy band, buy links, theme stylesheet) in config/config.json or the studio table — never inside a component.
Do give every interactive element a visible 2px Ember focus ring (focus-visible), and let the global CSS carry the browser chrome: color-scheme dark, ember selection and caret, thin token scrollbars.
Do frame catalog media in a portrait 3:4 inset tile with object-contain over the design's baked background color — nothing is ever cropped.
Do treat Poppins, Inter, and this palette as swappable defaults: build against roles (primary, muted, surface), not against specific values.
donts: Don't write a literal hex, rgb, or palette-utility color into a component — the token definition file, the form-status pair, and the themeColor meta value are the only sanctioned exceptions.
Don't introduce hues outside the token set; Ember is the only interactive hue, and green/red pairs are reserved for form success/error semantics only.
Don't animate hover with elevation, shadow, or decorative transforms — color shifts, fills, underlines, and the single sanctioned design-card image zoom only.
Don't put Poppins into body copy, controls, or labels — the display voice sings only in headings and card titles.
Don't sprinkle eyebrows onto ordinary content or stack white surfaces on the graphite field — panels are Panel-colored, one step up, behind a hairline.
Don't bake any single deployment's brand (name, monogram text, shop, imagery, hero copy) into a component — the product is white-label and every brand touchpoint is configuration.
